::: {.why}
The number you read off last night is the bar any backtest has to clear before it means anything, and it is higher than intuition puts it.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the expected maximum of N independent Sharpe estimates under the null, and how it grows with N.
- Say what correlation between the tried strategies does to that maximum, and in which direction.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>55 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Extend last night's simulation across N: for N of 10, 100, 1,000 and 10,000 null strategies, report the expected maximum realised Sharpe and its 95th percentile. Plot the expected maximum against log N and note that the growth is roughly proportional to the square root of the log.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Add correlation: repeat with the null strategies generated from a common factor so that they correlate at 0.5, and show the maximum falls. This is the effective-number-of-tests problem, and it is the reason a naive Bonferroni is conservative here for the same reason it is conservative across correlated variants in a scan.
:::
:::
